facts.claim: The SG/KR study specifies ten runs per scenario, agent and institute: 12 × 3 × 10 × 2 = 720 attempted runs, 360 per institute.
facts.population: three agents in twelve scenarios across two pipelines
facts.locator: physical pp4–10 scenario suite; p11 TableII repetitions and agents; TablesIII–IV run totals
facts.coordinateUse: Reproducible lower-level workload precedent for a pilot.
facts.limits: Not 720 valid scored outcomes: NA/terminated exclusions apply. No elapsed time, staffing, price or annual throughput is disclosed in these sections.

facts.claim: On the Singapore suite, SG pipeline fully safe-and-correct counts are A10/60, B35/60, C14/60; KR pipeline counts are A9/60, B21/60, C16/60.
facts.unit: fully safe-and-correct runs / 60 attempts per agent and pipeline
facts.locator: physical p11 Table III and p12 Table IV; read exclusions with metric definitions
facts.coordinateUse: Shows observed failure modes and pipeline sensitivity, motivating tests rather than assigning gate effectiveness.
facts.limits: Safe-and-correct is a joint endpoint, not leakage alone; these are not production rates or intervention/control effects. SG60-step cap and KR150-message cap differ.

facts.claim: GovTech describes chat.gov.sg red teaming using 21 attack skills and ten agents per policy, reducing the initially estimated 15% attack-success rate to 11.3% after audit; after guardrail changes none of the previously successful attacks succeeded.
facts.locator: attack-generation methodology, audit and guardrail-update results
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete historical remediation loop, stronger feasibility evidence than a plan alone.
facts.limits: No attack-count denominator, held-out set, cost or elapsed implementation duration. Retesting known attacks does not demonstrate zero new-attack risk or the proposed AISI leakage gate.

facts.claim: PSD and GovTech describe an HR agent using four binary quality metrics, synthetic conversations up to ten turns, restricted agency tool access, Litmus/Sentinel testing and owner remediation.
facts.locator: evaluation, tool filtering, failure feedback and phased rollout sections
facts.coordinateUse: Evidence that agency owners can integrate evaluation and fix defects before broader rollout.
facts.limits: Phased rollout remains subject to readiness/approvals; no nationwide compulsory gate, deployment population or test cost established.

gaps.field: binding release authority and exact leakage threshold/remedy
gaps.reason: Experiments and agency remediation exist, but no instrument delegates binding release control to AISI or sets this gate's threshold.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Obtain one agency's approved release checklist, delegated signatory and failed-test hold/retest rule.

gaps.field: eligible and covered production-agent inventory
gaps.reason: Case studies and award records do not enumerate all relevant production agents. Pair metrics were not recoverable; 90,490 is excluded.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Retrieve a dated agency agent register with active usage, model versions and release ownership.

gaps.field: marginal test cost, elapsed lead time and lab throughput
gaps.reason: Run counts and a safety-challenge contract exist, not gate-specific staffing, elapsed time or throughput.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Obtain run logs with elapsed time and compute cost plus itemised evaluator work orders.

gaps.field: production risk reduction caused by gate
gaps.reason: Experimental failure observations and known-attack retest success are not a controlled deployment-gate effect.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Use held-out adversarial tests and matched pre/post incident exposure after an observed failed-release hold.

coordinateReadiness.y: not ready: empirical test performance exists but production coverage and causal gate effect do not

facts.claim: FY2026 tiers provide 1,000/2,000/6,000 points. At 0.5 GPU-hour per point for training, these imply 500/1,000/3,000 GPU-hours; inference alternatives are 100m/200m/600m input OR output tokens.

facts.locator: physical p3, allocation tiers and conversion notes
facts.coordinateUse: Defines a measurable award-level resource pool once actual award/consumption ledger is obtained.
facts.limits: Not actual consumption or national compute supply. Input/output tokens are alternatives; never add them to GPU-hours. Queues and hardware heterogeneity matter.
